newsitem.title: USA: Digital Systems sees EPS at bottom of range.
newsitem.headline: Digital Systems sees EPS at bottom of range.

text.p: Digital Systems International Inc expects 1997 earnings to be at the "lower end" of analysts' expectations, while revenues are expected to rise more than 30 percent, company officials said on Wednesday.
Chief Financial Officer John Flavio said he expected earnings at the "lower end" of analysts' forecasts, which range from $1.20 to $1.30 per share.
Chief Executive Officer Pat Howard said he expected revenues for the telecommunications software company to grow "slightly better than 30 percent."
Their comments came at the American Electronics Association conference here.
Digital Systems was off 2-1/2 at 12-1/2 in heavy Nasdaq trading.
In 1995 the company earned $0.75 a share on revenues of $68 million.
On average, analysts expect the company to earn $1.00 a share in 1996, excluding a charge for a write-off, and $1.26 in 1997, according to First Call.
For the first nine months of 1996 Digital's revenues were $62.5 million, up from $48.4 million in the comparable year-earlier period.
Earlier this month the company announced plans to acquire ViewStar Corp for 3.9 million shares of stock in a deal expected to close by year-end.
"It's our goal, it's our commitment, it's our plan to make this non-dilutive," Howard told analysts and investors at the conference.
